title: Call insight: Your intake team is asking the same questions in the same or
campaign_name: Intake Triage: From Leaky Funnel to Signed Cases

touchpoints.action: Post the core insight with urgency math — hook with specific failure, show the money loss, end with a question that primes them for Day 3
touchpoints.content_snippet:
I analyzed 23 law firm intake processes last month.

73% treat a $4K PPC lead the same as a $400 organic caller.

That's costing them $255K+ annually.
touchpoints.call_to_action: None — just engagement expected in comments

touchpoints.action: Send a 'reply-all' style email to engaged commenters or warm audience segment — tell the story of the PI firm that found 3 slipped PPC leads in one month
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: The 90-second fix that recovered $255K

A PI firm I worked with pulled their intake logs.

3 PPC leads in March went unanswered for 8+ hours.

All 3 became referrals to competitors.
touchpoints.call_to_action: Soft: 'Want to see where YOUR intake is leaking?' (primes for Day 4)

touchpoints.action: Reply to top commenters from Day 1 post — add a micro-story about urgency detection (arrest date vs. consultation inquiry) showing the qualification difference
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Exactly. The difference is asking 'What's your timeline?' first vs. last.

One PPC lead had an arrest date in 72 hours. Intake asked about case facts first.

Lead hired someone else in 6 hours.

touchpoints.action: Send a short framework email — the 90-second urgency screen (arrest date, court deadline, representation status). No pitch. Just the template.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: The 3 questions that separate hot PPC from cold organic

Here's the urgency screen we built:

1. Is there a deadline? (arrest, court date, custody order)
2. Do you have representation? (yes/no/exploring)
3. Ready to move this week? (yes/no/maybe)
touchpoints.call_to_action: Soft: 'Reply with your biggest intake bottleneck — I'll send a specific fix'

touchpoints.action: DM commenters or email repliers from Days 2-4 — ask 1 qualifying question to surface their specific pain: 'Is your intake bottleneck speed, qualification, or something else?'
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Hey [Name] — noticed you engaged on the intake post.

Quick question: When a hot PPC lead comes in right now, what's the biggest delay before your team qualifies them?

touchpoints.action: Send a case study / proof email — show the before/after of a firm that implemented the urgency screen (use Mandall Law if they do intake this way, or describe a general 3-attorney PI firm pattern without a fake name)
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: How a PI firm recovered 47 lost leads with a 90-second screen

March: Intake averaged 6 hours to first contact on PPC leads.
Sept: Down to 22 minutes.

Here's what changed...
touchpoints.call_to_action: Soft: 'Want to see the exact checklist they use?'

touchpoints.action: Post a contrarian take — 'Your CRM isn't broken. Your lead routing is.' Show the cost of treating all leads equally (re-angle the $255K math from Day 1 with new data point)
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Most law firms have the right CRM.

They just don't use it to route PPC leads differently than organic leads.

Cost: 3-5 cases lost per month.

touchpoints.action: Send the 'cost of inaction' email — show what happens when a firm does NOTHING (lost revenue, competitor wins, intake morale). Make it emotional, not preachy.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: What happens on the days you don't fix intake

Every hour a PPC lead waits for first contact:

- 40% higher chance they call a competitor
- 6-8x longer to close (if you even get them back)
- Your intake team answers the same questions twice

This month alone, that's costing you...
touchpoints.call_to_action: Soft: 'Let's audit your intake in 20 minutes — no obligation'

touchpoints.action: Reply to Day 7 post — add a specific stat (73% from original content) and ask a poll-style question in the comment: 'Do you treat PPC the same as organic?'
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Quick poll in the replies:

Do your intake questions change based on WHERE the lead came from?

(Most firms say no. That's the problem.)

touchpoints.action: Send a 'quick win' email — one small change they can implement TODAY (90-second urgency screen or CRM tag by channel). Position as easy, low-risk, high-impact.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: One thing you can change in 30 minutes

Add a CRM tag: 'Channel: PPC' or 'Channel: Organic'

Then route them differently in your intake flow.

That's it. Do that, watch what happens.
touchpoints.call_to_action: Soft: 'I can walk you through it in 15 minutes if you want'

touchpoints.action: Post a myth-busting take — 'Your intake form isn't the problem. Your first 90 seconds are.' Show the difference between a qualification question and a data-collection question.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Your intake form asks 23 questions.

You need 3.

Everything else is just noise that slows you down on hot leads.

touchpoints.action: Follow-up DM to Day 5 responders — personalize based on their answer. If they said 'speed,' send the urgency screen. If 'qualification,' send the form template. If they didn't reply, ask if they want a 20-min audit.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Hey [Name] — you mentioned [their pain point] was slowing down intake.

I pulled together something specific for that. Worth 15 min to look at?
touchpoints.call_to_action: Soft but direct: 'Let's schedule a quick call to see where you're leaking cases'

touchpoints.action: Send a 'last touch' offer email — frame it as a free audit or 20-minute intake walkthrough. Urgency: 'Only running this for firms in [practice area] this month.' Include a specific time option.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: Free intake audit (only 5 spots left)

I'm doing free 20-minute walkthroughs for PI/family law firms.

We'll review:
- Where leads are slipping through
- Your current urgency screen (or build one)
- Exact ROI fix

Spots fill fast.

touchpoints.action: Send a final 'closing' email — make them choose. Either they say yes to the call, or you're moving on (but stay in the nurture sequence in case they re-engage). This is the last hard ask.
touchpoints.content_snippet:
Subject: Last spot available (closes EOD tomorrow)

I'm finishing up the free intake audits.

If you want to see where your firm is losing cases, book now.

If not, totally fine — just let me know so I stop emailing.
touchpoints.call_to_action: Direct: 'Yes, audit my intake' or 'No thanks, remove me'

conversion_trigger: Engagement on Days 1-3 (comment, email reply, DM response) OR click through the calendar link on Day 13 OR direct message asking for the audit
expected_timeline: 7-10 days to first call booking (Day 13-14 conversion typical); full nurture 14 days for cold engagement, 5-7 days for warm/engaged audience
